text:
Maya: quick flag — Sable-3B int4 bring-up is showing a quality dip vs Gemma-7B on our summarization suite. sending minimal diffs and notes. :frowning_face:
Devon: ugh, how big is the delta?
Maya: rough numbers from yesterday run: `rougeL: 0.68 -> 0.61`, `avg_f1: 0.72 -> 0.64`, latency roughly same. outputs look more extractive and sometimes cut tails.
Chris: any signs of rotary/headmix mismatch or token id offset?
Maya: noticed odd alignment in longcontext tests. prob with rotary freq normalization + our tokenmap. stack trace is noisy but see phase wrap hints.
Priya: can you paste the eval snippet? I'll kick a focused ablation.
Maya: pasted below — trimmed batch logs and sample tokens:
```
# eval summary (extract)
model: sable-3b-int4
bench: summarization-suite-v3
rougeL: 0.61
avg_f1: 0.64
ppl: 15.2
latency_p95_token_ms: 12.1
sample_out: "Long input... The company decided to..." -> truncated mid-sentence
notes: more aggressive eos truncation, shorter tails
```
Maya: also saw this in KV warmup trace: `kvcache position 1024 -> rotated indices mismatch` (attached snippet).
bench-bot: comparison job complete — baseline Gemma-7B-int6:
```
rougeL: 0.68
avg_f1: 0.72
ppl: 13.4
```
Devon: hypothesis: int4 quant + our proj-order (q,k,v layout) + rotary scaling yields higher effective phase error. Could explain truncation + extraction bias.
Chris: yeah + tokenizer differences? Was Sable converted with byte-fuse normalizer or did we use direct mapping?
Maya: converter used straight vocab remap (no nfkc), we did not apply soft-casing. Token counts match but we have several OOV merges around sentence boundaries.
Priya: plan: 1) run a quick A/B: disable rotary scaling (force scale=1.0) 2) run conversion with nfkc normalizer + re-eval 3) try int8 calibration to see if quantization level is amplifying the instability. I'll queue jobs.
Devon: add a variant where we re-order kvproj from qkv->kqv (cheap kernel change) — see if headmix alignment improves.
Maya: queued tests: job ids 4321 (rotary-scale=1.0), 4322 (nfkc remap), 4323 (int8 calib), 4324 (kvproj reorder). ETA ~ 2h for first results.
Chris: good. also capture logits around EOS tokens and prefix KV activations for head 3/5 — maybe headwise phase flips.
bench-bot: job 4321 finished: rougeL 0.65, avg_f1 0.68, ppl 14.1. partial improvement.
Maya: promising — rotary-scale tweak regressed less but still below baseline.
Priya: job 4322 (nfkc remap) running now.
Devon: if nfkc helps, probably token boundary merges were the main issue. if not, int4 noise + headwise phase still suspect.
Maya: also FYI — observed slightly higher clamp events in int4 GEMM (quant overflow clipping) in logs. attaching snippet.
Chris: okay let's let the nfkc run finish then try int8. If int8 gets us to parity, we know quant noise is culprit and we can tune per-head scale or export per-head quant stats.
Priya: adding checklist to thread: - capture per-head rotary cos/sin norms; - run a short eval with kv-zeroed warmup; - try per-layer bias correction during dequant.
Maya: thanks all. will post full diffs when 4322/4323 complete. cc @eng-ml :eyes:
